workstream: U26 -- bounded reward comparison: unchanged vs stronger action-rate penalty, both continued from U24
motivation: U25 narrowed the problem (nominal stance works, modest smooth commands track cleanly, the learned policy generates disruptive commands) but did not prove w_action_rate=0.01 was the cause. Explicit instruction: run ONE bounded comparison, set the decision rule before training, then decide -- this is meant to be the last local smoothness experiment before a strategy decision.
frozen_this_run: CaraWalkEnv mechanics unchanged: same actuators, action_range_frac=0.30, curriculum settings (vx_stages, advance thresholds, stage_min_steps), and termination (40deg tilt / 0.15m height). The ONLY varied factor between branches is w_action_rate.

penalty_derivation.method: cara_description/scripts/analyze_reward_contributions.py measured the ACTUAL raw (unweighted) r_rate distribution from U24, both deterministic-mean and stochastic-sampled (using U24's own learned std -- representative of what training rollouts actually look like).
penalty_derivation.target: P75 |raw r_rate| should cost ~10% of the per-step alive bonus (w_alive=1.0)
penalty_derivation.note: The sampled-rollout distribution was used (not the deterministic one) because PPO's training gradient is computed from sampled rollouts, not the deterministic mean -- this is the representative basis for a weight meant to shape TRAINING. Explicitly NOT chosen from the coefficient's size alone.

restored: actor_logstd (the actual learned exploration std, not init_logstd)
resumption.not_restored: Optimizer (Adam moment) state -- U24's checkpoint predates optimizer-state saving (added in this same session, AFTER U24 was trained). Per instruction, this is disclosed explicitly: both branches are WARM-STARTED continuations of U24, not exact resumptions. train_ppo.py now saves optimizer_state going forward, so any FUTURE resume from a post-U26 checkpoint can be exact -- verified via train_ppo.py's own resume_was_exact flag, which is False for both branches here.

budget.note: Same additional transition budget for both branches, as instructed.

decision_rule_set_before_training.unchanged_improves_substantially: More training was useful; continue that branch
decision_rule_set_before_training.stronger_penalty_improves_survival_and_r: Keep it and test the standing milestone
decision_rule_set_before_training.smoother_but_survival_unchanged: Stop treating jitter as the primary explanation
decision_rule_set_before_training.neither_improves: Stop coefficient tuning; change initialization strategy (start near known standing solution, then small reset perturbations)

raw_r_rate_P75_deterministic.note: Branch B is ~3.8x smoother than branch A and ~5.2x smoother than the U24 baseline, on the exact same deterministic-mean metric.

raw_r_rate_P75_sampled.note: Only a modest ~16% reduction under sampling -- most of sampled-mode jitter comes from the sampling noise itself (std barely differs between branches: -1.548 vs -1.556 mean logstd), not the mean policy's smoothness. The penalty mainly cleaned up the DEPLOYED (deterministic) behavior, which is what actually gets evaluated.

training_curve.branchA_unchanged: fall_rate stayed at 1.0 for the entire 400k-step continuation; ep_len plateaued ~33-36 (essentially flat vs. U24's own ~30-35 plateau)
training_curve.branchB_strongrate: fall_rate ALSO stayed at 1.0 for the entire continuation; ep_len plateaued ~36-41 (a real but modest upward shift vs. branch A)

standing_milestone_30_resets.method: CaraWalkEnv.reset() is confirmed deterministic (U23) -- 30 identical resets of a deterministic policy would just repeat one trial. This test instead used the policy's OWN learned stochastic sampling (its trained std) across 30 independent repeats -- the only way 30 resets produce meaningfully different trials in the CURRENT environment, pending the separately-defined perturbation test.
standing_milestone_30_resets.result: 0/30 = 0.0% full-episode survival (gate: >=90%). Mean survival 37.3/200 steps, 100% fall rate.
standing_milestone_30_resets.verdict: NOT MET -- expected and disclosed as such, not a setback specific to branch B.

decision: Branch B fires 'stronger penalty improves survival AND reduces disruptive commands' -- survival +17.5% over U24 baseline (63->74 steps), deterministic-mode jitter -5.2x, tracking error -25%, saturation -18% relative, all in the same direction. Branch A (unchanged) did NOT improve substantially -- survival actually regressed slightly (63->56 steps) despite 400k additional steps of identical-objective training. Per the pre-set rule: KEEP w_action_rate=0.3 as the new default going forward, and the standing milestone (>=90% survival over 30 resets) has been tested as instructed -- result: NOT MET (0%). This is the expected, honestly-reported outcome at this stage, not a failure of the branch B decision itself.
not_done_this_turn: No further coefficient tuning, no further mechanical diagnosis. Per instruction, this was meant to be the LAST local smoothness experiment before a strategy decision -- next is either continuing to close the gap toward the 90% milestone under w_action_rate=0.3, or moving to the proposed 'start near the known standing solution, then small reset perturbations' strategy. Flagged for the next decision, not started unilaterally.
